julebord.om: For the office Christmas party, the holiday pre-game and the Santa party. Safe to play with coworkers – but never boring.

items.t: Everyone who has talked for a whole minute before someone said “you're on mute”, drink.
Point at whoever says “I'll keep this short” and then talks for ten minutes. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Explain your job the way you would to your gran on Christmas Day. If the table doesn't get it, drink two.
Everyone who has microwaved fish at work, drink. Your colleagues haven't forgotten.
A toast to all the office plants that didn't survive the year.
Everyone who has signed off with just “Regards” and meant it passive-aggressively, drink.
Point at whoever is most likely to slip away tonight without a goodbye. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks now – while they still can.
Give a 20-second speech on why this is the best Christmas party ever. Get through it without laughing and give out three.
Tell us your most embarrassing work moment this year – or drink three.
Cheers to whoever carries the most work without ever getting the credit.
New rule: everyone points with their elbow. Use a finger and drink.
Whoever has been at the company the longest gives out three.
Everyone who has hit “Reply all” on something meant for just one person, drink.
Point at whoever will be buying their Christmas presents on Christmas Eve. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Do your best impression of the Teams ringtone. The table votes – not convincing enough, drink.
Which bit of work jargon have you started using at home? Say it – or drink two.
Cheers to IT, who've turned everything we broke this year off and on again.
New rule: everyone has to say “Merry Christmas” before they drink. Forget and drink another.
Whoever travelled the furthest to be here tonight gives out three.
Everyone who has been on a Teams call in a smart shirt and joggers, drink.
Point at whoever always has snacks in their desk drawer. The winner gives out three.
Give the person on your left a LinkedIn recommendation – out loud and completely straight-faced. Laugh and you drink.
What's the strangest thing you've done working from home with the camera off? Tell us – or drink two.
Cheers to the people who organised tonight. Without you, we'd all be sitting at home.
New rule: address everyone by job title – “Pass the salt, Head of HR?” Forget and drink.
Whoever has worked the most overtime this year gives out four. Well earned.
Everyone who has booked a fake meeting in their calendar just to be left alone, drink.
Point at whoever looks like they have strong opinions on how to load a dishwasher. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Make up your Christmas out-of-office – out loud and brutally honest. If the table laughs, give out two.
What's on your CV that you can really only sort of do? Answer – or drink two.
Cheers to everyone who's new this year – welcome to the gang!
New rule: raise your hand before you speak, just like on Teams. Forget and drink.
Whoever has the birthday closest to Christmas gives out three.
Everyone who has brought shop-bought cake to work and let people think it was homemade, drink.
Point at whoever is most likely to still be wearing the Santa hat in the taxi home. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Name everyone at the table. Miss one and drink two.
Round the table: everyone shares the strangest Secret Santa gift they've ever got. Whoever got the strangest gives out three.
Cheers to whoever always refills the coffee machine – and never gets thanked.
New rule: nobody says “work” until the next rule card. Say it and drink.
Whoever has the most holiday left this year gives out three. The rest of us want to know how.
Everyone who has a mug at work that nobody else is allowed to use, drink.
Point at whoever is most likely to go home in the wrong coat tonight. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Name five of Santa's reindeer in ten seconds – or drink two.
What was your first impression of the person on your right? Say it – or drink two.
Cheers to everyone working between Christmas and New Year – you're the real Santas.
New rule: check your work email before the next rule card and you drink two.
Whoever has the most Christmas decorations at home gives out three. Photo evidence required!
Everyone who read the party invite just to check the menu, drink.
Point at whoever is most likely to answer work emails over Christmas. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks – and turns off notifications.
Round the table: everyone says a bit of work jargon no outsider would understand. Whoever gets stuck drinks.
What's the most pointless meeting you've ever sat through? Tell us – no names – or drink two.
Cheers to everyone who's said “I can take that one” – and regretted it the same second.
New rule: “cheers” is now “thanks for a great collaboration”. Say “cheers” and drink.
Whoever has been to the most Christmas parties this year gives out three.
Everyone who still doesn't know what half their colleagues actually do, drink.
Point at whoever has taken the most photos tonight. Whoever gets the most fingers shows the best one – or drinks two.
Hum a Christmas song. The first to guess it gives out two.
What's the funniest thing you've seen at a Christmas party? No names. Tell us – or drink two.
Cheers to cake Friday – the most important meeting of the week.
New rule: every request must start with “as per my last email”. Forget and drink.
Everyone who has bought themselves a Christmas present “by accident”, drink.
Point at whoever knows every single verse once the carols start. The winner gives out three.
Finish the sentence “Next year I'm going to …”. The table votes – not believable, drink.
Which colleague would you most like to be stuck in a lift with for three hours? Answer – or drink two.
Cheers to the boss! If the boss is here, the boss makes a speech – ten seconds, tops.
Everyone who has bought their Secret Santa gift at a petrol station that same morning, drink.
Point at whoever spends triple the Secret Santa limit. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Say “Merry Christmas” in as many languages as you can in ten seconds. Fewer than three, drink.
Which Christmas present have you swapped without the giver knowing? Answer – or drink two.
Everyone who has told a colleague “we must grab a pint soon” without meaning it, drink.
Point at whoever is most likely to google something mid-argument tonight just to win. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Pitch an idea for next year's Christmas party in 15 seconds. The table votes: yes = give out three, no = drink.
Everyone who's off for the whole week after Christmas, drink. Everyone else, toast enviously.
Point at whoever has the best Christmas jumper tonight. The winner gives out three.
Compose the most passive-aggressive office-kitchen note you can – out loud. Make the table laugh and give out three.
Everyone who has said “I'm only having one” tonight, drink.
Point at whoever you can hear laughing from the other side of the open-plan office. The winner gives out three.
Read out the subject line of the last work email you sent – in your most dramatic voice. Or drink two.
Everyone who thinks turkey is the worst bit of Christmas dinner, drink. Turkey fans, shake your heads.
Point at whoever is most likely to drag the whole table onto the dance floor. The winner gives out three.
Defend Brussels sprouts for 20 seconds. Convince nobody and drink two.
Everyone who has opened their advent calendar ahead of schedule this year, drink.
Everyone who has quietly cheated at a family board game over Christmas, drink.
Everyone who was playing Christmas music before November this year, drink.
Everyone who has sent an email at 11 p.m. just so the boss would see the timestamp, drink.
Everyone who has walked straight past a printer flashing red, drink.
Everyone who has turned back at the door because someone else was at the coffee machine, drink.
Everyone who has switched tabs at lightning speed when the boss walked past, drink.
Everyone who has said “I'll take a look at it” and never did, drink.
Everyone who has been quietly annoyed that someone took “their” seat at lunch, drink.
Everyone who has sprinted to the kitchen after a “leftover sandwiches in the kitchen!” email, drink.
Everyone who has replied with a thumbs-up to get out of writing a proper answer, drink.
Everyone who has nodded along to an acronym in a meeting with no idea what it meant, drink.
Everyone who has forgotten a colleague's name and avoided saying it for six months, drink.
Everyone who has had mince pies from the office kitchen for lunch, drink.

vill.om: For the crew who know each other well and can handle almost anything. 18+.

items.t: Everyone who has been in a group chat about someone in this room, drink.
Point at whoever looks the most innocent but definitely isn't. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Who here would you call at 4 a.m. – and who would you never call? Answer – or drink three.
Everyone who has woken up to a payment from last night they can't explain, drink.
Show the last screenshot you took – or drink three.
Everyone who has sent “You up?” after midnight, drink.
Point at the most convincing liar here. Whoever gets the most fingers tells their best lie – or drinks three.
What's the biggest lie you've ever told this group? Tell us – or drink three.
Read out the last message you sent to a crush – in your best newsreader voice. Or drink three.
New rule: end every sentence with “… in bed”. Forget and drink.
Everyone who has been dumped by text gives out two. You've suffered enough.
Everyone drinks. If you've kissed someone in this room, drink two. No questions asked.
Cheers to all the bad decisions that turned into great stories.
Everyone who has unsent a drunk text before the other person could read it, drink.
Point at whoever has the worst ideas at 3 a.m. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Say who here you think talks about you the most. If they admit it, they drink – if not, you drink.
Have a staring contest with the person opposite you – using your most seductive look. First to laugh drinks.
New rule: nobody says “ex”. Say it and drink two.
Whoever has hosted the most afterparties this year gives out three. Thanks for having us.
Everyone who has used a dating profile photo that's more than three years old, drink.
Point at whoever has the most screenshots of other people's messages. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
What's the dumbest thing you've done drunk? The group votes – if it's too boring, drink three.
Give the person on your left your best flirty compliment – if they're up for it. A blush means you give out three. A laugh means you drink.
New rule: whoever says “drunk”, “tipsy” or “wasted” drinks.
Whoever got home latest last weekend gives out three.
Everyone who has stalked their ex's new partner while terrified of accidentally liking an old photo, drink.
Point at whoever says “just one drink” and is the last to leave the afterparty. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
What's the worst excuse you've used to get out of staying the night? Tell us – or drink three.
Do your best impression of someone here when they're drunk. If the others guess who, give out three. If not, drink.
New rule: everyone drinks with their other hand. Forget and drink another.
Everyone who googled someone here before meeting them tonight, drink.
Point at whoever is most likely to vanish with someone before 2 a.m. tonight. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
What's the most embarrassing thing you've bought online while drunk? Tell us – or drink three.
Let the group write you a new dating profile in 20 seconds. Read it out with a straight face – or drink three.
Pick a drinking buddy. Every time you drink until the next rule card, they drink too.
Everyone who has slept with an ex “just one last time”, drink.
Point at whoever is worst at keeping a secret. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks two.
What's the worst chat-up line you've actually used? Say it – or drink three.
Tell a drunk story in 30 seconds with one detail that's a lie. If the group spots it, drink.
Everyone who has walked home on a Sunday morning in last night's outfit, drink.
Point at whoever would most likely date someone just for their holiday home. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
What's the pettiest thing you've done after a break-up? Tell us – or drink three.
Talk about your ex for 30 seconds without saying anything negative. Can't manage it? Drink.
Everyone who has had a regular hook-up they've never once had dinner with, drink.
Point at whoever says “I'll pay you back” and never does. Whoever gets the most fingers settles up now – or drinks three.
Who in this group have you been most envious of – and why? Answer – or drink three.
Say three things you like about the person on your right – and one habit of theirs that annoys you. Or drink three.
Everyone who has been interrupted by a flatmate coming home too early, drink.
Point at whoever most likely has an ex in every part of town. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
What's the most awkward thing that's happened to you on a one-night stand? Tell us – or drink three.
Review your last date in ten seconds – with a star rating. Or drink three.
Everyone who has lied about how much they earn, drink.
Point at the most dangerous person to go out with when you've got an early start. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Everyone who has turned down plans with someone here and then been caught out on Instagram somewhere else, drink.
Point at whoever has the most chaotic dating life. Whoever gets the most fingers shares the latest episode – or drinks three.
Everyone who has let their parents pay for something this year they really should've covered themselves, drink.
Everyone who has sent a photo and regretted it the second it said “seen”, drink.
Everyone who has woken up next to a kebab they don't remember buying, drink.
Everyone who has borrowed the host's bedroom at a party, drink.
Everyone who has read a partner's messages without asking, drink.

bli-kjent.om: For freshers’ week, a new flatshare or the first party with new people. Nobody needs to know anyone yet.

items.t: Everyone who has gone in for a handshake while the other person went for a hug, drink. If it ended in a high five, drink two.
New rule: “what do you study?” and “what do you do?” are banned. Whoever asks drinks.
Point at whoever seems most likely to set up the group chat after tonight. The winner gives out three.
Whoever’s reading: say the name of everyone round the table and one thing you know about each. Get them all and give out three. Miss any and drink two.
Cheers to the host! Anyone who doesn’t know the host’s surname drinks an extra one.
Everyone who has said they live “just outside the city” about somewhere two hours away, drink.
What’s the weirdest summer job you’ve ever had? Answer – or drink two.
Point at whoever you think has the best story about how they ended up here tonight. Whoever gets the most fingers tells it – or drinks two.
Swap seats with whoever you’ve talked to least tonight. Ask each other one question before the next card – or you both drink.
Everyone who has said “sorry, what?” three times and then just nodded and smiled, drink.
New rule: before you drink, say the name of the person on your left. Wrong name: drink another.
Which app would you be most embarrassed for someone to see in your screen time? Answer – or drink two.
Everyone who has introduced themselves to the same person twice at one party, drink. If it happened tonight, drink two.
You and the person on your right have ten seconds to find something you both hate. Manage it and cheers. If not, drink one each.
If you all shared a flat: point at whoever would buy the loo roll without asking anyone to pay them back. The winner gives out three.
Whoever grew up furthest north gives out three. Whoever grew up furthest south drinks one.
Everyone who has turned up to a party too early and walked round the block to kill time, drink.
What did you buy with your very first pay cheque? Answer – or drink two.
Guess where the person on your left grew up. Right region: give out two. Right town: give out four. Wrong: drink one.
Everyone who has been at a party where the only person they knew left first, drink.
Cheers to everyone who came tonight knowing just one person – you know more now!
Point at whoever seems to know someone everywhere. Whoever gets the most fingers names someone they know in Lisbon – or drinks.
What’s the best decision you’ve ever made after a few drinks? Answer – or drink two.
Everyone who has made a new best friend in the queue for the loo at a party, drink.
Everyone with a different accent from whoever’s reading: say “I’m just popping to the shop” in your accent. The best one gives out three.
New rule: every time someone says your name, raise your glass. Forget and you drink.
Everyone who has danced all night with someone without ever finding out their name, drink.
Point at whoever would definitely put their hand up just as the lecturer says “that’s all for today”. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
What’s the coolest thing you’ve pretended you could do – on your CV or on a date? Answer – or drink two.
Show the last song you played. If the table finds it embarrassing, drink two. If someone else has it on a playlist, cheers with them.
Everyone who has already followed someone here on Instagram tonight, drink.
Round: everyone says their name and one thing they’re good at that nobody would guess. The best one gives out three.
Point at whoever seems like they’ve never camped at a festival. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks – or tells us about their first.
Everyone who has lived somewhere so small they could reach the fridge from bed, drink.
Learn the name of whoever’s sitting furthest from you. On the next card, cheers with them and say their name. Forget it: drink two.
What’s your most unpopular food opinion? Answer – whoever disagrees most drinks.
Whoever had the most recent birthday gives out two. Whoever’s birthday is coming up next drinks one – in advance.
Everyone who knows their neighbour’s cat’s name but not their neighbour’s, drink.
Point at whoever you think studies or works in something completely different from everyone else. Whoever gets the most fingers says what – and gives out two.
Cheers to student loans – the only ones who have ever truly believed in us.
Make up a secret handshake with the person on your right: a high five, a sound and a move. If the table likes it, you each give out two.
New rule: check your phone and you have to tell the table what you were checking – or drink two.
Everyone who has got through a whole holiday on “thank you”, “beer” and pointing, drink.
Which song makes you sing at the top of your voice when you’re alone in the car? Answer – or drink two.
Point at whoever you think has been to the most gigs this year. Whoever gets the most fingers names the best one – and gives out two.
Find something in this room that says a lot about the host. Explain why in ten seconds. The funniest explanation gives out two.
Everyone who has been asked for a fun fact about themselves and gone completely blank, drink.
New rule: you can only ask questions to people you didn’t know before tonight. Ask someone you already knew and you drink.
What flatmate habit has made you move out – or nearly? Answer – or drink two.
Cheers to whoever turned up first tonight – they got to see the host in joggers.
Everyone who has said “we should hang out!” to someone they never saw again, drink.
Point at whoever has talked to the most new people tonight. The winner gives out three.
Guess the star sign of the person on your left. Right: give out three. Wrong: drink one – and hear why that’s so typical.
What’s the most overrated thing about where you grew up? Answer – or drink two.
Everyone who puts pineapple on pizza, drink – and explain yourselves.
Ask the person on your right about the worst place they’ve ever lived. Retell it to the table in 20 seconds. Good story: give out two.
Whoever has the fewest unread emails gives out three. Whoever has the most drinks one per thousand – up to three.
Point at whoever seems like the type to say hello to everyone they pass on a Sunday walk. The winner gives out two.
Everyone says cheers in a different language or accent. The most convincing one gives out two.
What’s the best thing you’ve ever bought second-hand – and the worst? Answer – or drink two.
New rule: drinks in your left hand only. Get caught with it in your right and you drink – and say the name of whoever caught you.
Give the person on your left a nickname based on something they’ve told you tonight. If they like it, give out two. If not, drink one.
Round: everyone says what song they’d put on next. The table votes – the winner goes on, and whoever suggested it gives out two.
Everyone who has said “I’m terrible with names” tonight, drink. Ask again – it’s allowed.

hyttetur.om: For the crew at the cabin – from Friday arrival to the Sunday clean-up. Some rules last all weekend.

items.t: Everyone who has used an outdoor loo by headtorch with the door ajar, drink.
Point at whoever always dodges the washing-up. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks – and does it tomorrow.
Weekend rule: whoever says the word “cabin” for the rest of the trip drinks. Yes, it’s going to be hard.
Cheers to whoever planned this trip! Anyone who never replied in the group chat about it drinks an extra one.
Do an impression of a noise the cabin makes at night. If the table guesses what it is, give out two. If not, drink one.
Everyone who forgot something that was on the packing list, drink. If it was your sleeping bag, drink two.
Point at whoever claimed the double bed before anyone else had their shoes off. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
What’s the worst thing you’ve ever forgotten to bring on a cabin trip? Answer – or drink two.
Everyone who has paid into the kitty and is still waiting to be paid back, drink – on the kitty.
Everyone who has slept in a bunk bed and banged their head on the ceiling in the morning, drink.
Write a new house rule for the cabin in the guestbook – or on a note on the fridge. If the table likes it, give out three.
Everyone who has ever explained a word in a guessing game by saying the word itself, drink.
Point at whoever will fall asleep first tonight – probably on the sofa with their coat on. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Whoever carried the most in from the car gives out three.
Everyone who has promised to get up early for a hike – and didn’t, drink.
New rule: everyone talks about themselves in the third person. Forget and you drink.
Tell us about the worst cabin trip you’ve ever been on – no names. Answer – or drink two.
Point at whoever will be up first tomorrow making breakfast for everyone. The winner gives out three.
Everyone who packed more beer than clothes, drink.
Weekend rule: whoever takes the last cup of coffee without making more drinks two.
Give a 20-second weather forecast for tomorrow – in your most dramatic voice. If the table approves, give out two.
Everyone who has slept on an airbed that was flat by morning, drink.
Point at whoever cheats at board games and calls it “strategy”. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Cheers to cabin peace! Everyone puts their phone in the middle of the table until the next card. First to grab theirs drinks two.
Everyone who has spent ten minutes trying to light the fire and ended up with a room full of smoke, drink.
What’s the most pointless thing you packed for this trip? Show us – or drink two.
Point at whoever is guaranteed to say “we should do this more often” at some point this weekend. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Guess how many empty bottles are in the kitchen right now. Closest gives out two; furthest off clears them away.
Everyone who has flicked through a cabin guestbook and read out an entry from 1997, drink.
Weekend rule: whoever gets up first tomorrow picks their seat in the car home. No arguments.
Whoever has been to this cabin the most times gives out one for each visit – up to five.
Everyone who has arrived to find the off-licence shut an hour ago, drink – if there’s anything left.
Point at whoever packed like you were going away for three weeks. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Build a tower out of things on the table – no glasses – in 30 seconds. If it stands for five seconds, give out three.
Everyone who has fallen over on skis and claimed it was on purpose, drink.
Which cabin tradition from childhood do you miss – and which are you glad is gone? Answer – or drink two.
New rule: everyone talks quietly, as if the neighbours in the next cabin are asleep. Whoever gets loud drinks.
Point at whoever has done the most driving – and the least drinking – on cabin trips over the years. The winner gives out four.
Everyone who has worn earplugs on a cabin trip because of someone in this room, drink.
Weekend rule: whoever snores tonight makes breakfast. The burden of proof lies with whoever lay awake.
Put on the most cabin-ish thing you can find – wool socks, an anorak or a beanie – and keep it on until the next card. Refuse and drink two.
Everyone who brought their work laptop “just in case”, drink.
Cheers to the cabin owner – and to being invited back. Anyone who’s broken something here drinks an extra one.
Point at whoever has sent a photo of the view to the family group chat today. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Mountains or seaside – and what’s your silliest argument for it? Answer – or drink two.
Everyone who has hunted for signal with their phone held up over their head, drink.
Pick an object in this room. Everyone else gets five yes/no questions. If they don’t guess it, give out two.
Weekend rule: whoever loses a board game writes a guestbook entry on behalf of the winner.
Everyone who has eaten a chocolate bar on a hike and said “it just tastes better up here”, drink.
Whoever did the food shop gives out three. Whoever has only eaten it drinks one.
Point at whoever will be first to suggest “one more round” of cards at 3 a.m. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
What’s the most embarrassing thing that’s happened to you on a cabin trip – that you can tell here? Answer – or drink two.
Everyone who has driven to a cabin with the wrong address in the sat nav, drink.
New rule: whoever goes to the loo has to announce “just popping out to check the weather”. Forget and you drink.
Write a five-item packing list for the next trip – no phone. Forget loo roll and drink two.
Point at whoever has a packing list – in their notes app or laminated. Whoever gets the most fingers gives out three.
Everyone who has gone on a “quick” cabin trip and stayed an extra day, drink.
Weekend rule: shoes off indoors. Anyone caught in shoes drinks – and mops the floor.
Cheers to the kitty – may it balance on Sunday. Whoever’s keeping track gives out three.
Do an impression of a cabin owner giving the tour: “and this is the fuse box …”. Nail it and give out two.
Point at whoever takes longest in the bathroom in the morning – at a cabin with one bathroom. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
If you got snowed in for a week, who here becomes the leader – and who starts a mutiny? Answer – or drink two.
Whoever walked furthest today gives out one per kilometre – up to four.
Weekend rule: whoever goes to bed last tonight brings in the firewood tomorrow.

bursdag.om: For the birthday pre-party: the birthday person takes centre stage, and everyone hears the best stories.

items.t: Everyone who bought the present on the way here, drink.
The birthday person picks tonight’s DJ. Anyone who changes the song without permission drinks.
Give a 20-second speech for the birthday person – without saying “happy birthday” or “amazing”. Pull it off and give out three.
Point at whoever definitely forgot to buy a card. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks – and writes one on a napkin.
New rule: the birthday person doesn’t pour their own drinks. If anyone sees it happen, whoever was sitting closest drinks.
Everyone who has known the birthday person for more than ten years, drink. More than twenty: drink two.
The birthday person says who here they’ve known longest. You cheers – and that person shares their first memory of the two of you.
What did you think of the birthday person when you first met – and when did that change? Answer – or drink two.
Everyone who met the birthday person for the first time tonight, drink – welcome!
Cheers to the birthday person with a booming “hip hip hooray”. Whoever shouts quietest drinks an extra one.
Point at whoever is going to give a speech nobody asked for later tonight. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks – and practises.
The birthday person brings in a law for the rest of the night – and is the only one exempt from it. Break it: drink.
Everyone who has wrapped a present in newspaper or a carrier bag because they forgot wrapping paper, drink.
Tell us how you met the birthday person – in ten seconds. Good story: give out two. If not, drink one.
Everyone who has forgotten the birthday person’s birthday at least once, drink. If it was this year, drink two.
Birthday person: name the best thing that’s happened to you in the past year. Everyone who was part of it, cheers.
What’s the worst present you’ve ever received – and did you say thank you? Answer – or drink two.
Point at whoever has been to the most of the birthday person’s birthdays. Whoever gets the most fingers gives out one per birthday – up to five.
Everyone who has had a voice note over two minutes long from the birthday person, drink.
Find someone you didn’t know before tonight and find out how they know the birthday person. Introduce them to the table – manage it and give out two.
The birthday person points at whoever knows them best. Three questions from the birthday person: all right, give out three. Otherwise drink three.
Cheers to all the other birthdays we forgot this year.
Everyone who has said “I’m too old for this” this year, drink – and join in anyway.
Which story about the birthday person gets told at every single party? Tell it – or drink two.
The birthday person skips their drink on the next card – and can give it to whoever they like.
Point at whoever has definitely scrolled through the birthday person’s old photos looking for an embarrassing one. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks.
Everyone who has blown out the candles on someone else’s cake, drink.
Make up a two-line birthday rhyme about the birthday person – it has to rhyme with “cake”. If they approve, give out three.
The birthday person picks two people who didn’t know each other before tonight. They’re drinking buddies until the next card: if one drinks, both drink.
Everyone who has asked for “nothing” for their birthday and been disappointed to get exactly that, drink.
Cheers to the guests who didn’t know each other before tonight – and soon will.
Point at whoever has given the birthday person the best present ever. The winner gives out three.
The table guesses what the birthday person wants most right now. The birthday person decides – the right guess gives out three.
Everyone who has started the birthday song in the wrong key and never recovered, drink.
What’s the weirdest thing you’ve ever done on a birthday? Answer – or drink two.
Sing the birthday song like an opera singer or a metal vocalist – the birthday person chooses. Refuse and drink two.
The birthday person crowns tonight’s best outfit. The winner gives out three.
Everyone who has a photo of the birthday person on their phone that they don’t know about, drink.
New rule: say “happy birthday” every time you speak to the birthday person. Forget and you drink.
Point at whoever is bound to get emotional during the speeches tonight. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks – and finds the tissues.
The birthday person does an impression of someone in this room. If the table guesses who within ten seconds, that person drinks.
Everyone who has been to an afterparty with the birthday person that lasted until breakfast, drink.
Show the oldest photo you’ve got of the birthday person. The oldest one gives out three – the birthday person has a veto.
What’s the most expensive thing you’ve bought yourself “as a birthday present”? Answer – or drink two.
Cheers to the cake – or to there being no cake. Whoever was meant to bring it drinks either way.
The birthday person tells us about their worst birthday ever. Anyone who was there drinks.
Everyone who has argued with the birthday person about something completely trivial, drink. Still disagree: drink two.
Point at whoever will post the most photos from tonight. Whoever gets the most fingers drinks – and promises to ask before posting.
Predict the birthday person’s life in ten years – job, home and one bad habit. The best prediction gives out two.
The birthday person gives a sip to everyone who hasn’t said happy birthday yet tonight.
Everyone who has written “happy birthday!” in a group chat without knowing whose birthday it was, drink.
What’s one thing you’ve learned from the birthday person? Answer – or drink two.
